findings.description: The 20 ms limit for T_DIAG agrees with CON-SUP-103, but the configured execution limits allow 110 ms of application execution per 100 ms on the single processor if all tasks reach their limits. This excludes supervisor execution. No workload evidence establishes which execution times can occur together.
findings.requested_change: Record the schedulability question and identify the workload bounds needed to verify the configured schedule.

findings.description: CON-SUP-115 requires rejection of an unknown task. The item instead checks for a task that is not supervised, while SYS-CFG-001 defines a supervised task as one named in the configuration. An unsupported task entered into that configuration could therefore satisfy the definition used by the check.
findings.requested_change: Define the validity check against an approved set of supported task identifiers. Record an open point if that set cannot be determined from the inputs.

findings.description: The item requires the code check before supervised tasks are released. CON-SUP-107 requires the check before any task is released, and STK-SUP-007 requires it before the application runs. The current wording permits an application task outside the configured supervised set to start first.
findings.requested_change: Apply the startup code-check precondition to the release of every application task.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 defines the image boundaries, but neither the item nor the sources define what constitutes a passing image integrity check. OP-SYS-005 records the missing method and reference value, so the stated test lacks an independent expected result.
findings.requested_change: Once the integrity decision is approved, reference the criterion and reference-value contract that the test must use.

findings.description: The item requires the configuration CRC check before supervised tasks are released. CON-SUP-107 requires the check before any task is released, and STK-SUP-007 requires it before the application runs.
findings.requested_change: Apply the startup configuration-check precondition to the release of every application task.

findings.description: The polynomial in CON-SUP-107 does not uniquely determine the stored CRC-32. OP-SYS-005 identifies missing parameters, including initialization, reflection and final XOR. The same configuration bytes can therefore yield different expected CRC values.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved complete CRC convention and the bytes it covers so the test can compute the expected value independently.

findings.description: The item combines image coverage at startup and at runtime. A startup check can cover the complete image up to the CON-SUP-107 limit while the runtime check misses part of that same image.
findings.requested_change: Make coverage up to 1 MiB independently judgeable for the startup check and the runtime check.

findings.description: The startup release gate covers supervised tasks only. CON-SUP-107 requires the integrity checks before any task release, and STK-SUP-007 requires them before the application runs. With configurable supervision membership, the current gate leaves other application tasks free to start.
findings.requested_change: Extend the startup integrity release gate to all application tasks.

findings.description: The stated 11 s limit applies only to a 1 MiB image. STK-SUP-008 requires a bounded full pass while running, and CON-SUP-108 specifies a per-cycle segment cadence. The item leaves completion time unbounded for smaller supported images.
findings.requested_change: State a full-pass time bound for the supported image sizes using the cadence and upper bound in CON-SUP-108.

findings.description: STK-SUP-008 requires a repeat of the code integrity check. The item gives a timing criterion but lacks an approved integrity criterion and reference value. A test can time a pass without establishing that the pass recognized corrupt code.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved integrity criterion and image reference value for the runtime check.

findings.description: The item does not identify the boundaries of the two consecutive task periods. CON-SUP-102 starts supervision when startup checks pass, while CON-SUP-105 starts the reaction clock at the end of the alive window. Measuring from startup-check completion or from the first task release can yield different fault times.
findings.requested_change: Define the first and subsequent alive-window boundaries relative to startup and task releases. Record an open point if the inputs do not establish the alignment.

findings.description: The trigger waits for a task to begin late. CON-SUP-103 defines the configured start limit, and CON-SUP-105 measures the safety reaction from expiry of a timing limit. A task that remains unstarted after expiry can defer late-start detection until it eventually runs.
findings.requested_change: Define detection when the start deadline expires without a start, including how a start exactly at the allowed limit is treated.

findings.description: The phrase 'still executing at the expiry' leaves the case where completion and expiry have the same measured timestamp open to different interpretations. CON-SUP-103 allows execution up to the configured limit and defines an overrun as execution longer than that limit.
findings.requested_change: Specify the inclusive completion boundary and the detection outcome when expiry occurs without a completion by that boundary.

findings.description: CON-SUP-103 specifies a measurement resolution of 100 µs. The item permits finer resolution without an approved rule for how finer measurements are interpreted. That choice can change fault classification near a configured timing limit.
findings.requested_change: Use the specified resolution or obtain an approved decision defining how finer measurements are used for timing-limit comparisons.

findings.description: CON-SUP-104 checks checkpoints from tasks released in the cycle, but the item does not identify what observable event constitutes a task checkpoint. This matters for T_DIAG, whose permitted execution in CON-SUP-103 can extend beyond the 10 ms cycle in CON-SUP-101.
findings.requested_change: Define or reference the observable event that supplies each task checkpoint and specify how its arrival is assigned to a control cycle.

findings.description: The control-output deadline references CON-SUP-105 for every listed fault, but that decision gives no detectability instant for the configuration-range fault in CON-SUP-115. The item supplies no start event for measuring that case.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the timing reference for configuration-range faults, including the effect of the control outputs already being low during startup under CON-SUP-109.

findings.description: The status-signal deadline references CON-SUP-105, which gives no detectability instant for the configuration-range fault in CON-SUP-115. The item supplies no start event for measuring that case.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the timing reference for configuration-range faults, including the effect of the status signal already being low during startup under CON-SUP-109.

findings.description: The item combines maintaining the control outputs with maintaining the operational status signal. STK-SUP-009 and CON-SUP-109 distinguish the two observable functions. The controller can keep the actuators off while incorrectly indicating that it is operational.
findings.requested_change: Make maintenance of the control outputs and maintenance of the status signal independently judgeable in the safe state.

findings.description: CON-SUP-109 requires both control outputs to be low from any reset. CON-SUP-003 establishes GPIO availability, but the workproduct gives no feasibility evidence or open point for maintaining both external levels during reset, before supervisor code can act.
findings.requested_change: Record the feasibility analysis needed to establish the external control-output levels throughout each supported reset path.

findings.description: CON-SUP-109 requires the status signal to be low from any reset. GPIO availability in CON-SUP-003 alone does not establish that level during reset, before supervisor code can act. The workproduct gives no feasibility analysis or open point for that interval.
findings.requested_change: Record the feasibility analysis needed to establish the external status-signal level throughout each supported reset path.

findings.description: The wording triggers reset only if a refresh actually happens outside the window. It gives no reset outcome when refreshes cease entirely, the case called for by STK-SUP-005 and treated as a window expiry in OP-SYS-004 using CON-SUP-106.
findings.requested_change: Specify the hardware reset outcome when the upper window limit expires without a refresh, including when no later refresh is attempted.

findings.description: Both this refresh and the flow check in SYS-SUP-005 occur at the end of the control cycle under CON-SUP-104 and CON-SUP-106. The item leaves their order open, so a refresh could occur in the same cycle before a flow fault is evaluated, despite the healthy-task restriction in STK-SUP-005.
findings.requested_change: Define how the end-of-cycle health decision controls the refresh for that cycle.

findings.description: The refresh condition is true whenever no listed task fault has been detected since reset. That also covers startup before supervision begins and a retained safe-state latch after reset. OP-SYS-010 records that CON-SUP-106 does not define the watchdog policy in those states.
findings.requested_change: Specify the operating states in which the periodic window-watchdog refresh is required using the approved startup and latch policy.

findings.description: The obligation to refresh at intervals shorter than 100 ms applies whenever no listed task fault has been detected since reset. This includes startup and a retained safe-state latch, where the independent-watchdog policy is undecided under OP-SYS-010.
findings.requested_change: Specify the operating states to which the independent-watchdog refresh bound applies and the approved rule for the first interval.

findings.description: Stopping refreshes on a task fault can put the CON-SUP-106 window-watchdog reset ahead of the fault report and supervisor reset required by CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-112. The item gives no precedence for a fault detected near window expiry.
findings.requested_change: Resolve which action takes precedence and align refresh cessation with the approved fault-report and reset sequence.

findings.description: The reset request is triggered by entering the safe state because of a fault. For a startup integrity failure, CON-SUP-109 already holds all safe-state outputs low. The item gives no clear trigger or 20 ms origin for that case, although STK-SUP-010 and CON-SUP-110 call for reset recovery.
findings.requested_change: Define the reset-request trigger and deadline origin for a qualifying fault detected while the outputs already meet the safe-state condition.

findings.description: The permitted interval of up to 20 ms after safe-state entry can extend beyond window-watchdog expiry under CON-SUP-106 when SYS-WDG-005 stops refreshes. A hardware reset can preempt the software reset request and prevent the supervisor-reset sequence in CON-SUP-110.
findings.requested_change: Define the required reset path and deadline for faults detected near watchdog expiry after the precedence decision is approved.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 places transmission of the fault report after safe-state entry. The item constrains only transmission completion, allowing transmission to begin before the controller has entered the safe state.
findings.requested_change: Specify the ordering of safe-state entry, the start and completion of fault-report transmission, and the software reset request.

findings.description: Requiring report completion before a software reset request does not establish that the report can finish before a CON-SUP-106 hardware reset after refreshes cease. The required outcome under CON-SUP-110 is unresolved for a task fault close to watchdog expiry.
findings.requested_change: State the approved transmission outcome when the window watchdog can reset the controller during the fault-reaction sequence.

findings.description: The item uses 'consecutive supervisor reset' without defining how an intervening watchdog or other reset affects the count. It also leaves the start of the 60 s interval outside the normative text. Those choices change when the CON-SUP-110 latch is set.
findings.requested_change: Specify which intervening events break the sequence and define when the 60 s of fault-free operation begins.

findings.description: The item preserves the five classes from CON-SUP-111 but omits that classification is based on the reset flags. Its stated test could accept another basis for classification without checking the source of evidence required by CON-SUP-111.
findings.requested_change: Specify the reset flags as evidence for startup classification and identify any flag interpretation that still requires an approved reference or decision.

findings.description: CON-SUP-111 requires a startup message carrying the reset cause, but OP-SYS-002 records that its serial format is undefined. A verifier has no agreed framing or encoding for identifying the message and reading the cause.
findings.requested_change: Reference an approved startup-message format with framing and an encoding for each reset class.

findings.description: CON-SUP-111 requires the service tool to read the reset cause. CON-SUP-113 defines no response field for the cause and returns ERR for requests other than GET STATUS and GET FAULTS. The item has no approved service interaction that satisfies both decisions.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved service request and response carrying the reset cause, and reconcile them with the ERR rule.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 says the report is sent within 10 ms. The item does not say whether to time the first transmitted byte or completion of the terminating line feed. The rationale selects completion while OP-SYS-007 records the interpretation as undecided.
findings.requested_change: State the approved observable end event for measuring the 10 ms transmission deadline.

findings.description: The item requires a report within 10 ms for every detected fault. Under CON-SUP-106 and SYS-WDG-005, the window watchdog can reset the controller before that deadline and interrupt the report. The item gives no approved outcome for that case.
findings.requested_change: Define the report obligation when watchdog expiry can preempt transmission, using the approved reset precedence.

findings.description: SYS-DIAG-003 defines watchdog reset as fault code 8, and SYS-DIAG-002 requires an entity in every report. The item gives no entity for code 8 because the task, CODE and CONFIG values listed in CON-SUP-112 do not identify a watchdog reset.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved entity value for a watchdog-reset fault report.

findings.description: The entity for a flow fault is 'the affected supervised task.' Under CON-SUP-104, a cycle can have multiple missing or out-of-order checkpoints. CON-SUP-112 gives no rule for which task name to report in that case.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved task-selection and reporting rule for missing and out-of-order checkpoints, including when several checkpoints are wrong.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 gives the field as milliseconds since start without defining the time origin. The item selects the latest reset and uses 'the controller started' without identifying an observable event. OP-SYS-007 records the time origin as undecided.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved timestamp origin as an identifiable event and apply it to fault reports after each relevant reset type.

findings.description: STK-SUP-013 asks the service tool to read the last faults, and CON-SUP-113 calls for the last eight fault reports. The item limits history to reports already transmitted. A detected fault can therefore be absent from history if a reset interrupts its serial transmission.
findings.requested_change: Define when a fault report enters history and resolve whether an interrupted transmission affects its availability to GET FAULTS. Record an open point if a product decision is needed.

findings.description: The CON-SUP-113 response template leaves the legal state values and the meaning of fault count undefined. The request boundary is also undefined. A verifier cannot form a complete request or determine the expected response for a known state and fault history.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved request framing, state encoding and fault-count semantics.

findings.description: The 50 ms deadline in CON-SUP-113 does not identify when receipt is complete or whether the first or final response byte ends the measurement. OP-SYS-007 records these timing references as undecided.
findings.requested_change: Define the observable start and end events for measuring the GET STATUS response time.

findings.description: The item calls for returning the reports in history. CON-SUP-113 does not define their wire order or framing, or how to distinguish a complete response with fewer than eight records, including an empty history.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved record order, response framing and termination for zero through eight records.

findings.description: The 50 ms response limit from CON-SUP-113 does not say whether timing ends at the first byte or at completion of all returned records. The request-side timing event is also unspecified.
findings.requested_change: Define the observable start and end events for measuring the GET FAULTS response time.

findings.description: The request trigger has no operating-state qualification. A GET FAULTS request received just before a CON-SUP-110 reset may have its response interrupted, and the item also gives no outcome for requests received while the safe state is latched.
findings.requested_change: Specify whether requests are accepted while reset is pending and while the safe state is latched, and define the required outcome for an accepted request overtaken by reset.

findings.description: CON-SUP-113 specifies ERR for other requests, but the item gives neither an approved boundary for recognizing an unrecognized request nor a response deadline. The stated test cannot distinguish a missing ERR from a delayed one.
findings.requested_change: Specify the framing for unrecognized requests and the approved time bound for completing the ERR response.

findings.description: CON-SUP-114 ties the processor-use measurement to the configured core clock. OP-SYS-012 records that the clock setting is absent, and the item does not reference a controlled simulator configuration from which to obtain it. Different settings can yield different results.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved simulator core-clock setting or controlled profile used to reproduce the processor-use test.

findings.description: The item assigns execution of integration and system tests to the controller software. STK-SUP-015 and CON-SUP-116 require the controller to be testable in Renode and identify the environment for running those tests. They do not assign a test-runner function to the controller.
findings.requested_change: State the simulator compatibility required of the controller and place test execution in the verification environment.
